title: YonedaRepo: build together, keep the why
format: 12 scenes × 30 seconds. Existing capture filenames are historical and await lead refresh. Captions describe implemented behavior; they do not claim the images demonstrate the new features. No new funded-trial success, deployment, or browser acceptance is claimed.

scenes.title: A private key opens the prepared workspace
captions: A reviewer access key opens a dedicated sandbox without signup or a personal provider key.
The key stays private and can be revoked or allowed to expire.
A previously recorded checked run can be reviewed before deciding whether to start new work.
This walkthrough does not claim a new funded trial succeeded.

scenes.title: The checked CLI stays read-only
captions: Run node tools/reviewer.mjs --checked --no-open to inspect a recorded checked run without launching a browser.
The CLI reads paged run history and selected-run detail when the hosted service supports those routes.
A narrow compatibility path reads the legacy snapshot only when the service reports the repository operation is unknown.
Checked mode never starts a trial, resumes paid work, or calls a model.

scenes.title: New work uses Git-native forks
captions: New coding work uses scoped Git-native fork transport for canonical, candidate and task workspaces.
Older records created with JSON workspace transport remain readable as historical evidence.
The transport recorded for a run determines how its source and capture are interpreted.
This historical capture predates the refreshed transport view; it is not visual proof of the new path.

scenes.title: Repair reopens only the affected team work
captions: An owner can repair selected team tasks using the current plan revision and each selected task revision.
The ledger fences superseded attempts and reopens the selected tasks plus dependent work.
A repair brief becomes part of a new plan amendment; it does not rewrite the prior handoffs.
Repair is bounded to two rounds, after which the owner must choose another course.

scenes.title: Handoffs and integration preserve captured revisions
captions: A handoff is an agent assertion; trusted capture records the validated source revision separately.
Disjoint task outputs can be assembled from their exact captured revisions with a scoped file overlay.
The integration candidate records its source tasks and is independently evaluated after capture.
Ledger history distinguishes claims, captured files, checks and owner decisions.

scenes.title: Disjoint refresh creates a real two-parent merge
captions: When candidate changes are disjoint from the newer canonical head, trusted Git refresh merges both trees.
The refreshed candidate records the canonical head and original candidate revision as its two parents.
Refresh creates a new candidate revision and queues fresh independent checks against that revision.
The original candidate remains immutable evidence; refresh does not silently replace it.

scenes.title: Overlaps require an owner-approved resolver
captions: A true overlap remains unresolved with its paths and frozen three-way merge workspace recorded.
The platform does not choose a side or claim an automatic semantic merge.
An owner brief can authorize a scoped resolver that works from both parents and edits only approved conflict paths.
Its fresh capture and independent checks determine the resulting candidate's eligibility.

scenes.title: Preview and verification stay separate
captions: A preview serves static output from the exact candidate manifest on an isolated origin.
An independent evaluator checks the captured revision; passing checks make it reviewable, not published.
The repository admits at most six active work runs, with execution and model-request limits frozen into approval.
These bounds limit resource use; they do not demonstrate large-scale throughput or a new successful trial.

scenes.title: File lineage follows trusted captures
captions: Per-file receipts come from Worker-verified Git trees, not paths or blob IDs supplied by an agent.
A receipt records old and new blob IDs, capture identity, task revision and changes such as rename or deletion.
Unchanged files can inherit exact lineage through a verified refresh; changed files are attributed only to matching captured bytes.
When a file has no trusted receipt, the answer is explicitly unknown.

scenes.title: Why stays specific to the file
captions: A file-level why view follows that path's captures and inherited lineage across revisions.
It connects relevant context and decisions, including rejected alternatives and their recorded reasons.
Run-wide activity is not presented as proof of who changed a particular file.
Assertions, trusted capture, independent checks and the human shipping decision remain distinct.

scenes.title: A human still controls publication
captions: The owner reviews the checked revision and records a rationale before selecting it.
Selection and publication are separate states; the human decision remains the publication gate.
Publishing uses an expected-old Git lease, ancestry checks and remote readback.
The historical capture is awaiting refresh; this script does not claim a new trial or publication succeeded.

scenes.title: History is immutable and paged
captions: Terminal history can be archived into a digest-bound bundle; reads verify the stored bytes against that digest.
Run lists, graph context and large candidate diffs use bounded pages with stable cursors or watermarks.
The browser loads one run's detail first and hydrates graph context or diffs when requested.
Pagination keeps history review scoped instead of polling a full repository snapshot.
